---
name: ruler-evidence-researcher
description: Build or resume one reusable, local-first cited evidence dossier for a resolved political ruler and defined year or ruler-period, mapping stable evidence IDs to every applicable Leaders Database 1B-8B question without scoring. Use for ruler-level evidence collection, dossier continuation, evidence deduplication, question coverage mapping, and gap reporting before chapter-specific judging.
---

# Ruler Evidence Researcher

Build one durable evidence dossier per ruler-period. Do not run one research pass
per question and do not assign final comparative scores.

## Required inputs

Require a resolved ruler identity, ISO3 country, target year or bounded period,
output/checkpoint directory, question catalog, and local-prior package. Stop if
the case is identity-quarantined or the readiness report is not ready.

Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/methodology/local-first-researcher-guide.md`,
`docs/methodology/ranking-evaluation-criteria.md`, the applicable chapter
guides, and `docs/methodology/source-confidence-registry.json` before external
research.

## Workflow

1. Load the ruler identity, period boundaries, local facts, existing dossier,
   completed queries, and question coverage matrix.
2. Audit the supplied deduplicated local package before internet material.
   Record which stable local fact IDs are usable, contextual, or unused; preserve
   source observation IDs, years, warnings, and valid local-prior locators; and
   distinguish country/inherited baselines from ruler conduct. Candidate lens links
   are routing hints, not proof of direct support. Never refetch a dataset already
   represented locally merely to restate its numeric values, and never interpret a
   missing local row as a zero or favorable condition.
   Resolve compact disposition references when explaining missingness. Treat an
   `error` status as a blocking local-input failure and keep it visible in the
   handoff; internet evidence must not silently replace a broken extraction.
3. Work through chapters `1B` to `8B`, and their lenses, in order in the same
   researcher session. Begin with one broad ruler-period reconnaissance across all
   chapters and major source families. Before each lens, reuse and map the accumulated
   ledger first, then search only for remaining events, contrary interpretations, or
   attribution gaps. Continue until the chapter is reasonably saturated or further
   searching is unlikely to improve it; explain the stopping judgment.
4. Persist every accepted evidence item immediately under a stable evidence ID in the
   permissive notebook. A separate machine-readable ledger manifest is optional and must
   never block a substantive handoff when the execution profile cannot write files.
   Record the claim, source, URL, publisher, date, short excerpt, source type,
   source confidence, period fit, ruler attribution, and contrary evidence.
   Aim for 5–20 defensible source-claim units per selected chapter, with 10 as the
   normal target. One unit is one traceable source supporting one materially
   distinct claim; headings, excerpt fragments, empty priors, equivalent URLs, and
   repeated statements do not create new units. Normally retain no more than two
   units from one URL and justify exceptions. Report chapter mappings separately
   from independent locator/source families. This is a research-depth goal, not a
   publication gate: sparse or closed-information cases remain valid when the
   notebook records inspected candidates, rejection reasons, usable evidence, and
   the exact themes/source types still missing.
5. Indicate which chapter lenses each evidence item may inform. Natural mapping
   and coverage language is acceptable; the parent may normalize it later.
6. Checkpoint search queries, sources visited, evidence records, mappings,
   unresolved gaps, and run profile throughout the session. Resume from those
   checkpoints instead of repeating discovery.
7. After the initial notebook, respond to the evidence review in the same session.
   Search directly for every material gap selected by the reviewer, merge useful
   evidence into the register, and document gaps that cannot be improved. Repeat for
   at most three review rounds, stopping earlier when the reviewer passes the dossier
   or the researcher reports a reasoned saturation/blocker conclusion.
8. Produce a permissive research notebook/handoff before formatting. Record each
   source as it is accepted, including its reference, main-points summary, useful
   excerpts or locators, temporal fit, attribution, contrary points, and candidate
   chapter/lens links. Do not spend the research pass satisfying a strict final schema.
9. Finish only when each applicable question is marked `covered`,
   `partially_covered`, `no_evidence_found`, `not_applicable`, or
   `research_blocked` with a reason. Use `no_evidence_found` only after recording
   explicit searches and a specific explanation; absent formatter output is
   `research_blocked`, not evidence of absence.
10. Self-audit the register before handoff: empty priors never count; post-period
    material is context unless it establishes a target-period fact; same-source
    splits are non-independent; country/institutional evidence is not automatically
    ruler-attributable; and global IDs, chapter mappings, and reported counts must
    reconcile.

## Boundaries

- Treat the client matrix as validation-only, never evidence.
- Do not silently resolve ruler identity or expand the requested period.
- Do not invent citations, quotations, facts, usage, or token counts.
- Preserve one evidence record even when it maps to many questions.
- Record meaningful contrary evidence and closed-information-environment gaps.
- Use the provider/model selected by the parent run profile. Do not change model
  or provider inside the dossier.
- Internet search is an essential researcher capability. Do not accept a preselected
  link packet as a substitute for direct iterative research.
- Return a blocker rather than bypassing tool, credential, budget, or output
  restrictions.

## Handoff

Return a durable permissive research notebook and handoff. A separate formatter
may interpret natural-language headings, tables, JSON fragments, or prose and turn
them into the validated cited dossier. The downstream scientific unit remains one
chapter-year judge batch across all eligible ruler dossiers.

item.text:
## Research continuation handoff — Clark / New Zealand / 2000

Direct searches recovered several defensible units and clarified multiple attribution limits. No score is assigned.

### Added or repaired evidence units

- **EV-1B-R2-A — NPT 2000 consensus outcome**  
  The NPT 2000 Final Document states in Part I, paragraph 15, that the Conference agreed on practical steps for systematic and progressive implementation of Article VI; item 6 records the “unequivocal undertaking” to eliminate nuclear arsenals. Part II, paragraph 31, records adoption of the Final Document by consensus on 19 May 2000.  
  Locator: Final Document PDF, Part I p.19, paras. 15 and item 6; Part II p.34, para. 31.  
  Source: UN conference record, high confidence.  
  Attribution: establishes the international outcome, not Clark’s individual causal role.  
  Links: 1B.1, 1B.4, 1B.10.  
  [UN NPT Final Document](https://app.unidir.org/sites/default/files/2020-09/2000%20NPT%20RevCon%20Final%20Document_1.pdf)

- **EV-1B-R2-B — New Zealand’s disarmament posture**  
  The 2000 NPT record supports the substance of the disarmament outcome, while the existing Clark speech remains self-attribution rather than independent proof that New Zealand secured it. Retain the Clark speech only as direct evidence of her public position, not as proof of causal credit.  
  Limitation: no independent source located in this round tying a specific Cabinet instruction or Clark negotiation to the final consensus.

- **EV-2B-R2-A — East Timor deployment performance**  
  The Auditor-General concluded that the NZDF “for the most part met its obligations well” in responding to the Government’s decision to participate in East Timor; planning was “intense, flexible, and responsive,” and the force was assembled and deployed within government-set times.  
  Locator: report PDF, pp.21–22, paras. 2.2–2.4.  
  Source: Office of the Auditor-General, high confidence.  
  Attribution: Cabinet-authorised operation; supports government execution, not necessarily Clark’s personal conduct.  
  Contrary evidence: the same report says some preparations and operations could have been better performed and records lessons for improvement.  
  Links: 2B.1, 2B.4, 2B.9, 8B.6, 8B.7.  
  [OAG East Timor audit](https://oag.parliament.nz/2001/east-timor/docs/timor.pdf)

- **EV-2B-R2-B — Operational risk and accountability**  
  The audit states that NZDF planning and deployment required management of varied risks and examined systems directly affecting the Government’s decision, preparedness, mobilisation, deployment, public accountability, and financial management.  
  Locator: report PDF, pp.33–34, paras. 3.5–3.9.  
  Source: OAG, high confidence.  
  Attribution: institutional/Cabinet-level accountability; does not establish that Clark personally directed operational choices.  
  Links: 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9, 8B.7.

- **EV-2B-R2-C — Public acknowledgement of risks and mission purpose**  
  In her 18 November 2000 Labour Party Conference speech, Clark described East Timor as “hot, dangerous,” involving risks of serious illness and death, while stating that the work was helping give the new nation a start.  
  Locator: speech paragraphs on East Timor and Bougainville, immediately following the APEC discussion.  
  Source: Beehive primary speech, medium-high confidence.  
  Attribution: direct PM statement.  
  Limitation: public framing, not an independent outcome assessment.  
  Links: 2B.1, 2B.5, 2B.6, 2B.7.  
  [Clark, Labour Party Conference 2000](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/speech/address-labour-party-conference-2000)

- **EV-3B-R2-A — 2000 police activity record**  
  The New Zealand Police Annual Report 2000 covers 1 July 1999–30 June 2000 and records policing of major national events including APEC security, state visits, Y2K, and the America’s Cup.  
  Locator: report landing page, “Annual Report 2000” description.  
  Source: New Zealand Police, medium-high confidence.  
  Attribution: institutional activity only.  
  Disposition: context, not proof of Clark-directed restraint or misconduct.  
  Links: 3B.2, 3B.8, 3B.10.  
  [Police Annual Report 2000](https://www.police.govt.nz/about-us/publication/annual-report-2000)

- **EV-3B-R2-B — Calendar-year crime data availability**  
  Police published official recorded and resolved offence statistics for the calendar year ending 31 December 2000. The publication explains that the figures are drawn from the Police National Intelligence Application and define recorded and resolved offences.  
  Locator: publication page, paragraphs under “Crime Statistics for calendar year ending 31 December 2000.”  
  Source: New Zealand Police, high confidence for data provenance.  
  Attribution: country outcome data, not Clark attribution.  
  Disposition: context/local-outcome support only; do not infer safety improvement without examining the tables.  
  [Police crime statistics 2000](https://www.police.govt.nz/about-us/publication/crime-statistics-calendar-year-ending-31-december-2000)

- **EV-4B-R2-A — Direct PM engagement with Treaty institutions**  
  Clark’s Waitangi Day speech identifies her presence at Ōnuku marae and explicitly acknowledges Crown failure to fulfil Treaty obligations, while calling for continued courage and wisdom in addressing contested Treaty issues.  
  Locator: speech opening and Treaty-history paragraphs.  
  Source: Beehive primary speech, high confidence.  
  Attribution: direct PM statement and personal attendance.  
  Contrary evidence: the speech demonstrates recognition and engagement, not measurable institutional reform or absence of coercion.  
  Links: 4B.1, 4B.7, 4B.10, 6B.3, 6B.8.  
  [Waitangi Day Speech, 6 February 2000](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/speech/waitangi-day-speech)

- **EV-5B-R2-A — 2000 unemployment forecast and adverse fiscal context**  
  Treasury’s BEFU 2000 forecast approximately 162,000 unemployment recipients in 1999/2000, falling to 153,000 in 2001/02; it forecast unemployment declining from 6.4% to 5.4% over that interval. This is a forecast, not an observed 2000 outcome.  
  Locator: BEFU 2000, pp.31–32, “Community Wage – unemployment,” lines describing recipient numbers and unemployment rate.  
  Source: Treasury primary, high confidence.  
  Attribution: macroeconomic context under the Government; not solely Clark.  
  Contrary evidence: the forecast implies continuing substantial unemployment and is partly post-period.  
  Links: 5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.10.  
  [Treasury BEFU 2000, Fiscal Outlook](https://www.treasury.govt.nz/sites/default/files/2007-09/befu00-2.pdf)

- **EV-5B-R2-B — Budget health and education spending**  
  Treasury projected health spending rising from $6.873bn in 1999/2000 to $7.236bn in 2000/01, including new policy initiatives, and education expenses rising over the forecast horizon with new school and tertiary funding initiatives.  
  Locator: BEFU 2000, pp.32–33, lines under “Health spending” and “Education.”  
  Source: Treasury primary, high confidence.  
  Attribution: Cabinet budget framework.  
  Limitation: forecast expenditure is not proof of realised household welfare or service quality.  
  Links: 5B.6, 6B.1, 6B.2, 8B.2, 8B.6.

- **EV-6B-R2-A — 2000 tertiary participation and persistent disparity**  
  The Ministry of Education’s *Profile & Trends 2000* reports approximately 265,000 formally enrolled tertiary students at 31 July 2000 and a 4.2% year-on-year increase. It also reports that Māori and Pacific students remained under-represented: only one in ten Māori school leavers from 1999 entered university in 2000, compared with more than one in four overall.  
  Locator: report webpage, “Summary,” lines describing data coverage; “Student Participation and Achievement,” paragraphs on enrolment and under-representation.  
  Source: Ministry of Education, high confidence.  
  Attribution: observed national outcome; no direct Clark attribution.  
  Contrary evidence: persistent disparity limits any claim that Closing the Gaps had already produced equal access in 2000.  
  Links: 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.8, 6B.10.  
  [Profile & Trends 2000](https://www.educationcounts.govt.nz/publications/80898/profile__and__trends_2000_new_zealands_tertiary_education_sector)

- **EV-6B-R2-B — Closing the Gaps monitoring mechanism**  
  The Budget 2000 release states that Te Puni Kōkiri would audit Māori government programmes and receive $2.175m in operating funding for 2000/01 to establish an effectiveness-audit function covering health, employment, housing, and education.  
  Locator: Beehive page, paragraphs beginning “The quality of government programmes…” and listing Te Puni Kōkiri funding.  
  Source: Beehive primary, high confidence.  
  Attribution: Cabinet programme design; direct PM/Cabinet responsibility is stronger for the funding decision than for later results.  
  Links: 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.9, 8B.5, 8B.7.  
  [Budget 2000 — Closing the Gaps](https://www.beehive.govt.nz/feature/budegt-2000-closing-gaps)

- **EV-7B-R2-A — Independent confirmation of the GE Royal Commission’s timing**  
  The Ministry for the Environment records that the Royal Commission on Genetic Modification was established by the Government on 8 May 2000. This confirms the target-period institutional setting for the later GE-corn controversy but does not confirm Hager’s cover-up allegation.  
  Locator: publication page, establishment paragraph.  
  Source: Ministry for the Environment, high confidence.  
  Attribution: Government/Cabinet institutional action; no direct evidence of Clark’s knowledge of the contamination.  
  Links: 7B.1, 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.9.  
  [Royal Commission on Genetic Modification](https://environment.govt.nz/publications/report-of-the-royal-commission-on-genetic-modification/)

- **EV-7B-R2-B — Limiting evidence on Corngate**  
  The official Royal Commission source establishes the commission’s creation and later report, but the material retrieved does not independently adjudicate whether Clark knew of, directed, or concealed the GE-corn response. Hager’s account and NZ Herald reporting therefore remain adverse allegations, not findings.  
  Disposition: retained as an attribution-limiting source note, not positive or negative proof of personal dishonesty.
